answer: When an AI‑agent marketplace registers new participants it requires each node to submit a cryptographic proof tied to a physical‑world credential, such as a signed sensor reading from a unique karst cave humidity sensor. The system aggregates these proofs into a weighted bridge graph; only agents that contribute distinct walnut‑shaped noise patterns to the graph earn voting power, and any cluster that tries to mimic another identity fails the cross‑validation step, forcing the attacker to purchase and operate separate real sensors.
